pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - Clubs
pageCache.text:
Clubs
Clubs take place throughout the school year and may be at lunchtime or after school. We offer a diversity of clubs that recognise the great range of talents and interests that Epsom Downs Primary children have. Clubs may include gymnastics, dodgeball, netball, choir, football and writing but change on a termly basis. You will be informed about the clubs on offer at the beginning of every term and your child can sign up for their preferred option. Please note that places are limited and are offered on a first-come first-served basis.

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - About BASH
pageCache.text:
About BASH
Our breakfast, after school hub BASH is a popular provision that has been running since 2008. It offers affordable childcare to children in full time education from full time reception to Year 6, run by experienced activity leaders.
Breakfast
Breakfast club starts at 7:45am and offers healthy breakfast options including cereal, toast and fruit juice.
The children have some free play time and eat their breakfast before we do the Wake Up Shake Up routine to leave them full of energy and ready to learn.
Children attending Breakfast Club should be dropped off at the Family Centre, St Leonards Road entrance.
After school
Afterschool Club runs from 3:10pm to 6:00pm, with the option of a shorter session from 3:10pm to 4:30pm, available five days a week.
It gives children the opportunity to take part in a number of activities such as sports, arts & crafts, cooking, music and dance.
We have a snack each evening all eating together to chat with our friends. These snacks are healthy and include things like, Sandwiches, Wraps, Pitta bread with a choice of different fillings! In the colder months we also have Jacket Potatoes and Soup. Each evening fruit and water are also available to have.
Children attending the After School Club must be collected from the the Family Centre, St Leonards Road entrance.
Car Park
Please do not use the car park at the St Leonards Road entrance when dropping off and collecting your children as it is pedestrianised as part of our one way system.
For all enquiries and bookings, please ring 07873 224011 or email bash@epsomdowns.surrey.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - English
pageCache.text:
English
Reading at Epsom Downs
Early Years Foundation Stage
Language and literacy activities are built into the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum and are an integral part of all learning alongside personal, social and emotional development and physical development. Activities such as singing, story-telling, craft and outdoor learning help to reinforce development in these skills and increases every child's understanding of the world around them.
Phonological awareness and rhyming activities, singing and listening to stories are considered essential for children’s literacy development. Letters and Sounds, phase 1 is introduced through rhyme time and stories with children. Core rhymes and stories are a feature of the literacy learning in the Foundation stage and offer rhyme, rhythm and repetition; prompt cards and prop boxes are being developed to ensure an environment rich in language and words. This feature extends into year 1. Practitioners know how important stories are and take great pleasure in reading stories to children (individuals and groups). In the summer term, Nursery are introduced to the phonemes through our RWI scheme and this continues into Reception, where children will read books using their phonics knowledge.
Key Stage One and Key Stage Two
Read, Write, Inc is the programme we use to help children learn to read and spell sounds in words. The books they read link to the sounds that they know. Children in certain year groups will be bringing home Read, Write, Inc Book-Bag books. Children so enjoy the opportunity to share a book with an adult that they know or love.
The reading expectation at Epsom Downs is that children in Rainbow Unit and KS1 will read for 10 minutes a day; those in KS2 will read for 15 minutes a day. Daily reading needs to be recorded in this planner with a comment and signature.
Read Write Inc. Phonics is a whole-school approach to teaching literacy for children aged 4 to 9 that creates fluent readers, confident speakers and willing writers. Interactive lessons full of partner work, role-play and drama integrate phonics with comprehension, writing, grammar, spelling, vocabulary and handwriting. Your child will be re-assessed in reading every 6 to 8 weeks to track his/her progress.
Read Write Inc. Spelling is a 15-minute-a-day programme for Years 2 to 6. Using a proven approach underpinned by phonics, fast–paced lessons and an online subscription, Read Write Inc. Spelling prepares children for the higher demands of the statutory spelling assessments in England. Your child will be assessed in weekly tests throughout the year.
Read Write Inc. Fresh Start is a catch-up and intervention programme with proven results for 9 to 13-year-olds still learning to read. A proven pedagogy and step-by-step approach gives students the skills to read accurately and fluently with good comprehension, to spell correctly and compose their ideas for writing step-by-step.
Read Write Inc. parent information
Listening to your child read
Year 1 Phonic Screening Check
Whole Class Guided Reading:
Guided reading is planned for weekly by class teachers, using high quality core texts, many that match our wider curriculum. Texts have been chosen to inspire, engage and excite our children across a range of genres. The language within our core texts is rich and varied, exposing children to high quality sentence types, which we firmly believe also supports their writing. Guided reading sessions comprise the following:
Reading for pleasure:
We passionately advocate reading for pleasure. We have a superb, well-stocked library with a huge range of literature: contemporary and classic fiction, non-fiction, graphic novels, diversity and inclusion and picture books. We also have a wide selection of book-banded books aimed at readers of all levels. Children will go into the library frequently to change their reading books to take home to share and classes plan library sessions where children read for pleasure together in the calm environment of our reading tent. We have a yearly Book Week which is a much-anticipated week of fun based on a chosen text. Parents are invited in to read as families during this week and teachers also plan paired reading sessions, where children of mixed year groups share books together. We have very strong links with a local care home – Rosebery Manor where we take some children to read to the elderly residents. This is a lovely opportunity to share our love of reading with our wider community. We have the Scholastic Book Fair in several times a year where children can buy from a wide range of books. Funds raised from these fairs provide hundreds of pounds-worth of free books for our school.
Every week, each teacher/ TA in the Early Years and Key Stage 1 hears each child read. This is recorded in home learning planners with targets recorded accordingly. Parents are supported to read with their children at home through the use of regularly changed school books, home-school communication in home learning planners and newsletter updates. TAs are also deployed effectively to support children’s reading. Throughout KS2, children are given opportunities to read to an adult or independently. Children who are reading at a level below their age-related expectation will be listened to more frequently to support their fluency and comprehension.
The IDL Literacy Intervention is a speaking-computer-based multi-sensory system which supports learners to increase their reading and spelling ages. Individual children will be given a login for this programme if s/he needs to practise. Your child’s login is in his/her planner.
Writing
Our writing approach across the school is called ‘I Am A Clever Writer’ (IAACW). It is an approach based on the key skills children need to learn in each year group and has explicit progression so that these key skills are thoroughly embedded and built upon year-on-year. These key skills are always visible in the classroom so that children know explicitly what makes them a ‘Clever Writer’.
Our Working Walls always support our writing by displaying key elements of our learning throughout the week.
Every class has a set of high-quality core books that cover a variety of genres and topics – always linking to our wider curriculum. These genres also include picture books, poetry, non-fiction texts and film clips or shorts. All have been carefully chosen to stimulate interest, passion, creativity and scope for teaching or embedding the specific key skills.
Text and media examples across the school:
Teachers use these resources to write a ‘model example’ text which is shared with the children to start the week. The key skills within the model text are discussed and the children are introduced to high quality, advanced vocabulary (Star Vocabulary), often assigning actions to help define them. The model text is always ambitious and challenging, but accessible to all our learners.
Every day, with each piece of writing, teachers and TAs are live-marking. Children are being exposed to instant feedback as they write. Adults have important conversations with children about how well they have used a skill, but they also discuss improvements that need to be made to ensure essential skills are used correctly. Basic skills, handwriting and spellings are always a focus. By using the live-marking approach, teachers are immediately aware of how to move the learning forward and children can experience bespoke learning, as feedback is tailored to their immediate needs.
Our units of writing are usually one or two weeks long and the expectation is that children will write every day. Not only will children write every day – they will have resources prepared (if necessary) to ensure that they are independent writers, no matter what their ability. All children are able to be successful with the IAACW approach.
The week finishes with a ‘Star Write’ – a final piece of extended writing showing all the skills that have been taught or embedded during the week. There is always great excitement on ‘Star Write’ day as children are very keen to showcase their ‘Clever Writer’ skills, with many pieces being displayed around the school and with children sharing their successes.
See examples below of Star Writes across the school, from the start of our writing journey in Reception through to Year 6:
Our IAACW approach is fostering a love of writing across the school allowing our children’s creativity to flourish and their confidence to soar as they become adept at using their tools to make them real-life writers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - PSHE
pageCache.text:
PSHE
Personal, Health and Social Education underpins life at Epsom Downs Community School. Our school is a values-based school that believes in developing a set of skills and attitudes that prepare our children for the modern-day world. Children’s attitudes to themselves and each other must be healthy if they are to be safe, happy learners. The emphasis is on encouraging individual responsibility, awareness and informed decision making, which is based around our seven school values of resilience, empathy, self-awareness, positivity, excellence, communication and teamwork. Our school PSHE Curriculum aims to provide opportunities for all pupils to learn and achieve. It promotes pupil’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural development and prepares children for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of life.
Our curriculum also fully covers the statutory aspects of the Relationships Education and Health Education in the Department for Education’s Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education Statutory guidance
Our PSHE Curriculum links to our whole school curriculum intent, since it is:
Engaging – children learn through child-centred, engaging themes. The themes are from the Jigsaw PSHE teaching material and are exceptionally relevant to the changes, pressures, situations and circumstances that children at Epsom Downs are likely to experience as they grow up.
Enriching because the thematic content enriches children’s lives; empowering them to have a progressively better understanding of the health and well-being, their relationships and how to live well in the wider world.
Values-Centre because our Epsom Downs values - Respect, Resilience, Empathy, Self-Awareness, Positivity, Excellence, Communication and Teamwork - and British values, underpin all that we teach in PSHE.
Language-rich - At Epsom Downs, we recognise our children come from a diverse community and the need for our children to be introduced to and taught specific vocabulary about their feelings, thoughts and emotions. This language is embedded and developed throughout PSHE lessons, developing in complexity with each year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - Enrichment
pageCache.text:
Enrichment
Enrichment in our Curriculum
We are proud of the large number of enrichment opportunities that we give our children. These opportunities make our school wonderfully unique, go well above and beyond the National Curriculum expectations and are always well received and enjoyed.
Healthy Body, Healthy Mind (Yr 1-4)
Children develop their understanding of health by exploring exercise, nutrition, hygiene, and body awareness, while also learning about emotions, friendships, conflict resolution, and personal safety. They are introduced to mindfulness practices and gain awareness of people who help us and emergency procedures. In computing, they build foundational digital skills, progressing from logging on and using a keyboard to word processing and touch typing.
Children learn to care for animals safely and responsibly, understanding their needs, habitats, and characteristics. They take part in feeding, cleaning, and general farm maintenance, while exploring the roles of preventative care and human-animal teamwork. They discover where food comes from, identify animal types and baby names, and discuss the environmental impact on wildlife.
The children learn how to stop, move off and change direction without skidding. While riding their bikes, they demonstrate an awareness of space by judging distances and by navigating through a restricted space. They also learn how to control their bikes when facing an oncoming rider and how to use their brakes correctly and safely. Practise includes manoeuvring their bike around various obstacles. The children are shown how to check their bike and helmet and adjust to their needs before riding.
Children develop key cookery skills by following recipes, practising hygiene and safety in the kitchen, and learning to measure ingredients accurately using scales and cups. They use techniques like rubbing in, mixing, rolling, and cutting to create dishes such as omelettes, muffins, and pizza. Alongside practical skills, they explore healthy eating and proper use of kitchen tools and equipment
In our new art lessons, children explore a variety of techniques and materials to express their creativity and develop their artistic skills. Each unit introduces them to different styles, tools, and artists, encouraging experimentation and personal interpretation. As they build confidence, children learn to observe closely, use colour and texture effectively, and reflect on their own and others' work. The lessons aim to make art enjoyable and accessible, nurturing imagination, self-expression, and a deeper appreciation for visual creativity.
Both Art, and Animals will incorporate elements of gardening next year
Children explore a different sport every other half-term, focusing on developing new skills and techniques in a fun, engaging way. Activities are tailored to individual ability, helping children build confidence, teamwork, and an understanding of rules. As they progress, they enhance their physical, social, and communication skills, and are gradually introduced to more competitive play.
Computing (Yrs 5 and 6)
Computing lessons are delivered by specialist teachers from Junior Jam, offering children exciting, hands-on experiences with technology. Through engaging, innovative activities, children learn to compose digital music, create their own apps, and explore coding and multimedia tools. These lessons build essential digital skills while encouraging creativity, problem-solving, and confidence with technology in a fun and inspiring way.
Forest School (Year 6): Year 6 children take part in Forest School sessions designed to build confidence, resilience, and teamwork through outdoor learning. Set in our beautiful Headley Drive Nature World, they engage in hands-on activities such as shelter building, fire lighting, and tool use, all while developing a deeper connection with nature. These sessions encourage problem-solving, independence, and an appreciation for the outdoors in a safe, supportive setting.
Swimming (Year 5): Year 5 children attend weekly one-hour swimming sessions at Tadworth Leisure Centre, where they learn a range of swimming strokes and develop their technique in the water. The programme also includes vital water safety and lifesaving skills, helping children become confident, capable swimmers. The sessions are tailored to different abilities, ensuring all children make progress and gain essential life skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - School Trips and Workshops
pageCache.text:
School Trips and Workshops
School trips are a vital part of the curriculum and we encourage children to attend wherever possible. We seek out the most stimulating school visit opportunities that bring the children’s learning to life, enabling them to explore new environments and ask questions about what they have seen. Recent visits have included Winchester Planetarium and Science Centre, Bodiam Castle, The British Wildlife Centre, Littlehampton Beach, Gatton Park, Butser Ancient Farm and residential trips to High Ashurst and Hindleap Warren.
We also have a number of in-school workshops during the year - recent topics have included Stone Age Day, Great Fire of London, Egyptian and Greek workshops.
We do not exclude children from school visits and workshops on financial grounds, so please do contact the school office if you would like to discuss your ability to contribute. Please be assured that all conversations will be conducted in confidence.
Summary of all Trips and Visitors

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - Art in the Community
pageCache.text:
Art in the Community
In collaboration with Epsom Arts Society, we are displaying work from Epsom Downs Community School at Tattenham Corner Train Station.
We have chosen to display the Year 2 art work, based on the work of Paul Klee
They used the idea of Klee’s piece ‘Castle and Sun’ to inspire them. They used 2D shapes to create the castles and sun then used water colours for the background and poster paints for the castles. The children learnt how to mix colours for their pieces of art work.
We hope you enjoy looking at the pieces as much as the children enjoyed creating them.
Sponsored by The Arts Society Epsom

pageCache.pageTitle: Epsom Downs Primary School & Childrens Centre - Head Teacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head Teacher's Welcome
It is my pleasure and privilege to welcome you as you visit the Epsom Downs Community School and Early Years Centres website. We are a very unique educational establishment with a Day Nursery (which offers childcare provision for babies from 3 months); BASH club (Breakfast, After school and Holiday Club); Family Centre; two classes from Nursery up to year 6; a specialist High CoIN (Communication and Interaction Needs) centre; a farm; bio globe; 2 nature worlds; 2 outdoor eco classrooms; sports field with pavilion. Please take your time to walk through our website and find out more about the entire provision we offer. I hope you will get a feeling of the wonderful learning environment we will provide for your child and I trust that you find the information both useful and informative.
At Epsom Downs Community School, our guiding motto is "Learning Together; Succeeding Forever." At the heart of our educational philosophy lies a strong emphasis on relationships. We firmly believe that a nurturing and supportive environment is essential for your child's success. Our central conviction is that children who feel happy and secure will not only thrive but also achieve their full potential.
We are committed to fostering an atmosphere where learning is a collaborative journey, and every child is encouraged to explore, discover, and grow. Our dedicated team is here to provide a well-rounded education that not only focuses on academic excellence but also on the overall well-being of your child.
We believe that we are a unique school, catering for children from 0-11 years of age, during which time we really get to know all of our children and help them on their individual learning journeys. To achieve the best start we aim to support each child to achieve more than they ever thought was possible and to develop strong, supportive and respectful relationships with each other and the adults they work with. We have high expectations of all children and provide them with the challenge, opportunities and support for them to flourish. Through an engaging, creative curriculum that links knowledge, skills and outdoor learning opportunities, children are given the chance to further develop their self-esteem, problem solving and collaboration skills through hands-on learning in a natural environment.
We have a strong, dedicated team, who are passionate about ensuring the best start in life for all children. The senior leadership team drive the school in a cohesive direction, a member of this team is on the playground every morning as a point of contact for parents. Within this team we have phase leaders across the school who ensure consistency and high expectations across each key stage. Every teacher, teaching assistant and member of the admin and premises team, act as role models in order for children to achieve the highest standards.
Please click here to view our five year vision statement which is focused around the strapline:
Learning Together: Succeeding Forever
We strive to work closely with parents as we know it is when school and home life combine that children achieve their very best, please click here to see the results of our latest parents survey.
We hold many events and sessions throughout the year where parents are invited into school. Keep a look out on the diary dates and newsletter for these events.
Thank you for visiting our website. To find out more about us and our intentions and strategies contact the office on 01737 354313 to arrange a tour.
